/catalog/: Compare custom boxes, bags, pouches and printed accessories by construction and intended use. Each reference includes a local product image and details to discuss for your own specification. Use the PHG reference when requesting dimensions, materials, printing and a sample. Catalog orders start at 500 pieces.
/catalog/paper-boxes/: Compare folding cartons, corrugated mailers, presentation boxes and carry boxes. Begin with the complete contents, opening routine and packing method, then review board, dimensions and any insert. A printed exterior does not establish transit performance. Confirm the assembled sample and the final construction for your order.
/catalog/bags/: Compare paper mailers, carrier bags, product bags and flexible pouches by their actual construction. Choose the opening, base and intended packing or carrying task before selecting materials and print. For filled pouches, specify the contents and filling route; for parcel or gift bags, review the complete packed item.
/catalog/packaging-accessories/: Complete a packaging range with cards, tags, labels, sleeves, dust covers and displays. Match the printed component to the product or pack it will accompany. Presentation and container references require the supplied component to be identified before quoting; a staged image does not establish a fixed stock product.
951346153: Explore packaging references from across the collection. The range includes different structures and applications, so use the product details and format collections to compare like with like. Confirm the actual component, dimensions, material and print before requesting a quotation or approving a matching sample.
917683989: Use these packaging ideas to start a structural and artwork brief. Identify which pictured components belong in your order and which are only styling or contents. Compare the relevant format, then share measurements, quantity per design and delivery country so the quotation refers to one clear specification.
920016676: Compare mailer and shipping-box references around the packed contents and delivery route. Review internal dimensions, board, closing method and any insert or protective layer. Printed branding and opening features should work with the parcel arrangement. Agree the relevant sample and handling checks for the complete pack.
950338332: Review kraft and corrugated mailing references with the product they will carry. Confirm the actual liner, board construction and printed surface separately from the image's color or finish. Compare dimensions, closure and packing clearance on a formed sample; a kraft appearance alone does not establish parcel protection.
950338333: Plan the printed mailer as both a parcel and an opening experience. Compare the outside shipping surface, inside presentation panels, label positions and closure. Confirm the board, dimensions and packing arrangement before decorative finishing. Review the print on the selected liner and the formed box.
951398518: Compare mailer references whose opening brief may include a tear strip. Confirm the strip position, opening sequence, closing method and whether a separate return closure is required. Identify these features on the drawing and try them on a packed sample rather than assuming them from a product photograph.
951662766: Review the complete box, insert and packed-product arrangement for the intended delivery conditions. Compare board, dimensions, closure and working clearance around product corners. Protection must be evaluated for that complete system; the category name and a neat sample image are not transport-test results.
919910675: Compare paper carrier and mailing-bag directions around their different jobs. Carrier bags require a review of handles, base and loaded comfort; mailing bags require parcel clearance, seams and closure. Confirm the paper and finished dimensions with the actual item before selecting print or finishing.
952968758: Plan a paper carrier around the complete retail purchase, including its product box and any wrapping. Compare usable opening, gusset, base, handle drop and attachment. Review the loaded sample and printed surface together. Paper weight or a rope-handle appearance alone does not establish the finished bag's carrying limit.
952857851: Compare paper mailing bags as parcel envelopes. Review usable interior, seams, closing flap and any opening or return strip with the actual packed goods. Reserve space for delivery labels and confirm handling requirements for the route. These references are mailing formats rather than paper shopping bags with carrying handles.
803631155: Compare gift-packaging references by opening and presentation, from folding structures to rigid boxes. Identify the actual construction on the product page before selecting material, insert or finish. Review the full set and the recipient's opening routine on a matching sample. Branded contents shown in images are not supplied.
953980869: Review magnetic presentation-box references as a board, wrap, lid and insert system. Confirm the closing arrangement and whether the box is supplied assembled or flat. Check loaded lid alignment, product access and print across the opening sequence. The final magnetic configuration belongs on the approved construction drawing.
953294826: Compare drawer-box references around sliding clearance, pull access and the contents being presented. Specify the outer sleeve, inner tray, dimensions and any insert separately. Review the loaded drawer and print alignment on a formed sample before approving the final board, wrap and artwork.
954034112: Compare lift-off-lid presentation directions around the lid overlap, tray depth and complete contents. Confirm board, wrap, usable dimensions and insert requirements on a matching sample. Review how the recipient removes the lid and product, and check the artwork on the assembled box.
952891404: Review tube-box references by diameter, height, lid arrangement and the product being packed. Confirm internal clearance and any support separately from the decorative wrap. Check placement, removal and the formed tube with a suitable sample. The photograph does not identify the full wall construction or final dimensions.
954038904: Explore shaped and presentation-focused paper packaging. Identify the actual opening, folds, board and supplied components before choosing a decorative finish. A specialty shape can change usable space and packing steps, so compare the product with a matching physical sample rather than relying on the staged image.
921840222: Coordinate boxes, product bags, mailers and printed pieces around the actual apparel item. Compare folded dimensions, protection, opening and the retail or delivery task. Confirm materials and print for each component and keep quantities separate when an order includes both product packaging and an outer parcel layer.
953294833: Compare flexible product-bag references around the item, usable opening and closing method. Review film, thickness convention, seams and clarity with a packed sample. Distinguish a protective or retail bag from an outer shipping mailer. Printed material or environmental claims require confirmation for the final construction.
954067551: Review reclosable product bags by zipper position, usable interior and the item being packed. Confirm the opening profile and any final seal separately. Check insertion, repeated access where required and film contact with the actual contents. A zipper reference does not by itself define a standing base or parcel-shipping performance.
954072335: Compare poly mailing bags as outer shipping envelopes. Specify film, opacity, finished dimensions, seams and adhesive-flap arrangement around the complete parcel. Review label space and any return strip on a packed sample. Confirm handling checks and the protection required by the actual goods and delivery route.
954038909: Review box directions for apparel and underwear presentation around the full folded item or set. Confirm the construction, usable dimensions, opening and any window or insert. Printed themes shown in the examples are artwork references. Use a matching sample to compare packing and customer access before approving the final specification.
952983140: Compare printed tags and attachment directions around the actual product. Confirm finished size, paper, hole position, string or other fixing and printed faces. Review how the tag hangs, whether codes remain readable and how it contacts the item. Approve the final wording and attachment with a physical sample.
803708590: Build a cosmetic packaging brief around the actual container, formula or complete presentation set. Compare cartons, boxes and supporting components by their role. A secondary paper box is different from a directly contacting refill pack; confirm the material and application requirements for each component separately.
810538305: Compare food-packaging directions by construction and contact role. Identify the food, any inner liner or tray, fill quantity, packing conditions and delivery task. A presentation box, printed sleeve and directly contacting pouch require different specifications. Confirm the exact material and supporting information before approval.
920318966: Review sushi and meal presentation boxes around the complete tray or inner arrangement. Compare compartment layout, usable space, lid access and the intended packing or delivery routine. Confirm direct-contact components separately from the printed outer box and review the actual food arrangement with a matching sample.
953304411: Compare counter and floor-display references around product dimensions, facings, load and replenishment. Confirm the assembled footprint, shelves, dividers and header before arranging the graphics. Review a loaded sample and its shipping or assembly method. A display image does not establish a shelf-load rating.
920803216: Compare packaging directions for a tea project by format, fill quantity and the role of each component. Specify the actual tea, packing route and storage requirements for a contacting pack; review a secondary carton or gift box separately. Printed tea artwork does not qualify a laminate or establish shelf life.
920793609: Coordinate candle cartons, presentation boxes, sleeves and removable dust covers around the actual vessel. Review fit, opening, printed information and any outer parcel arrangement separately. A dust cover is a printed packaging component rather than a rigid box. Confirm every component and its approved artwork with the candle owner.
807897313: Compare cards, tags, booklets and other printed paper pieces around the information they must carry. Specify size, paper, printed sides, folding or cutting and attachment where needed. Check wording, codes and actual-size readability in the complete pack. Use dedicated sleeve and dust-cover collections for those structures.
803759676: Plan labels and stickers around the application surface and method. Confirm finished shape, material, adhesive, backing or roll supply and artwork. Review placement, readability and the intended removal or exposure conditions on the real product. The appearance of a label on its liner does not prove final adhesion.
919632767: Compare flexible pouch references by base, opening and intended filling task. Stand-up, flat-bottom, side-gusset, flat and fitment formats need different drawings and sample checks. Confirm complete material construction, dimensions and actual contents separately from the printed design. Shelf life, contact suitability and filling performance require project-specific review.
0: Explore additional packaging presentation directions. Identify the physical component and its intended task before comparing materials or print. Use the format collections and product reference to prepare a clear brief, then confirm supplied items, dimensions and sample needs in the written quotation.
pouch-stand-up: Compare bottom-gusset pouch references around the actual contents and fill quantity. Review finished dimensions, headspace, opening and filled standing behavior on a matching sample. Material, barrier requirements and printing are separate decisions; the stand-up shape alone does not define a laminate or establish capacity.
pouch-flat-bottom: Compare flat-bottom references as a base and panel system. Confirm the footprint, face and side dimensions, top opening and filled shape. Review how the chosen product fills and how packs fit in a secondary carton. The same nominal weight does not set the dimensions for different powders, beans or irregular contents.
pouch-side-gusset: Review gusseted bags by face width, expanded side folds, seam and top-closing arrangement. Confirm the actual base conversion rather than assuming a flat-bottom format. Compare a filled sample with the intended product and packing routine, then approve the dimensions, material, opening and artwork together.
pouch-spout: Compare fitment-pouch references around the intended contents and dispensing action. Specify bore, cap, position, fill route and final closing method. Liquids and dry granular products require different flow and sample checks. Confirm the film and complete fitment assembly for the actual formulation, fill quantity and handling conditions.
pouch-flat: Compare flat bags, pouches and sachets by usable area, seal pattern and opening. Identify the actual item or fill and how it enters and leaves the pack. Confirm material and final closing method on a matching sample. A flat reference does not automatically establish a bottom gusset, zipper or standing function.
pouch-specialty: Review shaped and nonstandard flexible-packaging directions by their actual conversion. Confirm the outline, seals, any folds, opening and intended contents before selecting a material or print route. Some references illustrate several configurations, so identify one final structure and approve a matching sample rather than assuming a conventional stand-up pouch.
folding-cartons: Compare paperboard cartons around product fit, panel layout and the actual flap or base construction. Confirm usable dimensions, board, grain, scoring and closing method on a formed sample. Review print and finishing on the selected surface. A gift theme or cosmetic illustration does not turn a folding carton into a rigid presentation box.
handle-carry-boxes: Review boxes with carrying features as a complete loaded structure. Confirm the board, handle position, attachment, base and opening around the actual contents. Compare lifting, handover and customer access with a sample. These are carry-box references rather than flexible paper shopping bags.
pillow-boxes: Compare curved-end folding pillow-box directions around usable interior space and the actual product. Specify the flat drawing separately from formed dimensions, then confirm paper, seam and end engagement. Review graphics across the curved panels and try folding, packing and opening on a matching sample.
beverage-straw-pouches: Review beverage-pouch references showing straw access and top finger openings. Confirm the insertion point, top sealing arrangement, any reclosure and the filling route separately. This opening style does not establish a screw-cap spout. Trial the intended beverage, straw and carrying method with a matching filled sample.
gift-carry-bags: Compare gift and carrying bags around the packed item, opening and carrying method. Confirm the actual fabric, paper or film before selecting seams, handles, cords and print. Review loaded access and handling with a matching sample; a presentation image does not identify a fiber composition or carrying limit.
roll-bags-liners: Review roll-supplied bags by individual bag dimensions, film, opening, base seal and perforation. State total bag count separately from bags per roll and roll count. Confirm core or coreless supply, dispensing and export packing with a sample. The reference is roll supply rather than a premade standing pouch.
bag-in-box: Define the liner, dispensing fitment and supporting outer box as separate components of one system. Identify what the quotation includes, then confirm filling route, fitment, filled liner and carton fit together. The photographed outer box does not specify a hidden liner or establish compatibility with the intended liquid.
presentation-container-references: Use these staged presentation and container images to define the packaging component you need. Confirm whether the request concerns a container, printed label, sleeve, wrap or presentation accessory. The image does not establish a flexible pouch, fixed stock specification or the availability of every pictured component.
packaging-sleeves: Compare printed sleeves and wraps around the underlying product, tray or plain package. Confirm wrap length, face panels, folds, overlap and closing method on the actual object. Review information visibility and fitting before approving print. A sleeve is a separate printed component rather than a complete shipping box.
candle-dust-covers: Plan removable printed candle covers around the vessel opening and wick arrangement. Confirm the cut outline, paper, any slot or removal tab and approved wording. Review placement and removal in the complete retail presentation. The printed cover is a packaging component, and reference-image instructions are not automatically approved candle information.
